A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same signature-kernel conditional-independence and SDE causal-discovery work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-D support reliable comparison despite the changed title, reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B and D report original SDE simulations, independence-test evaluations, functional-data experiments, partially observed graph recovery and stock pairs-trading results.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices B and D, including numerical comparisons and power analyses.

M1.justification: The signature-kernel CI procedure, Algorithms 1-3 and Appendix D's partially observed discovery procedure are retained. Moving the partial-observation discussion into the methodology and explaining the lifted graph do not introduce algorithmic changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same linear, nonlinear, path-dependent and diffusion-dependent SDE scenarios, missing observations, latent confounding, fractional Brownian motion, functional data and stock pairs trading.

E2.justification: CCM, Granger, PCMCI, Lau and SCOTCH retain their roles in the corresponding experiments; the trading comparators and kernel-test variants also remain. Additional SCOTCH rows in v3's Table 2 reproduce configurations already compared in v2's Table 8.

E3.justification: The SDE parameter ranges, trajectory counts, graph sizes, missingness procedures, trading splits and evaluation metrics are unchanged. The expanded main-text SCOTCH table redisplays existing configurations rather than documenting a new evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The kernel-bandwidth and interval comparisons, test-variant analysis, missingness robustness, causal-building-block tests, post-processing comparison and SCOTCH sensitivity analysis already appear in v2. V3 retains their evidence without adding analyses.

E5.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their mean/standard-error reporting and stated repetition, bootstrap, permutation and Monte Carlo counts. V3 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation practice or seed reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 3-9 retain their numerical results. Table 2 preserves its existing results and copies two SCOTCH configurations from v2's Table 8. Empirical plots and the partially observed experiment's 88-versus-8 false adjacencies per 100 runs are also unchanged.

T1.justification: V3 adds an explicit true-edge-preservation argument to the proof of Theorem 3.2, formerly Theorem 3.3. Appendix A.7 formalizes faithfulness and states that weaker parent faithfulness suffices. These are localized theoretical refinements; the main Markov, consistency and cyclic-counterexample arguments remain.

C1.justification: The central CI-testing and graph-recovery contributions remain, including partial-observation recovery already present in v2. However, v3's abstract and conclusion state soundness/completeness with a CI-oracle qualifier while omitting v2's explicit faithfulness qualification; Section 3.1 still requires faithfulness.

C2.justification: V2 acknowledges SCOTCH's large-graph advantage and suggests error propagation as a weakness of its own algorithms. V3 removes that explanation, advocates judging SCOTCH by worst-case hyperparameter performance, and argues for broader SigKer superiority from unchanged results. It also expands the faithfulness discussion and claims weaker parent faithfulness alleviates practical concerns.

D1.justification: V3 Appendix A.4 explicitly specifies an ordinary RBF kernel for tests involving single-time-point variables, such as initial values. V2 already uses such variables but does not disclose this kernel detail. The remaining implementation settings and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds focused references on faithfulness, including Andersen, Uhler et al., Weinberger and Mogensen (2024), plus Lee and Oberhauser on signature kernels. Several background citations, including Reisach et al. (2021), disappear. The central positioning within continuous-time causal discovery remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, experimental discussion and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Related work now leads with causal discovery, partial observations enter the methodology, and the appendices gain a contents list and reordered subsections.

P2.justification: V3 adds Figure 2 illustrating the lifted graph and expands Table 2 using existing appendix results. It changes typography and float placement, including wrapping text around Algorithm 1 and relocating the power plot. The existing empirical graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit proof direction, faithfulness discussion and lifted-graph illustration improve clarity. However, unchanged results receive stronger superiority claims, the error-propagation limitation disappears, and SigKer is called free of hyperparameter choices despite Appendix B.1 documenting parameter selection. These gains in exposition and losses in qualification leave the net quality change uncertain.
